taxonomic_note: POWO accepts Bidens frondosa L. Source pool iNaturalist taxon 51712. Do not confuse with compound-leaved B. vulgata.
look_here_first: FIRST photograph an ENTIRE middle stem leaf still attached at its OPPOSITE node: B. frondosa is usually compound, each leaf divided into THREE distinct serrated leaflets (sometimes five), each leaflet with its own little stalk; don't count opposite leaves as 'leaflets.' SECOND look under its small orange-yellow DISK HEAD for an outer ring of ~5–8(–10) green CALYCULUS bractlets and inner involucral phyllaries. B. vulgata can also have 3–5 leaflets but usually ~10–16(–21) outer bractlets: count these on an intact mature head. THIRD verify flattened mature cypselae with typically TWO barbed awns, about 5–7 mm outer / 7–10 mm inner bodies. Flower rays normally absent or tiny (0–3), but not a foolproof color test.

morphology_keys.habit: Annual herb, often branching, frequently in moist or disturbed habitats.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite on stem, petiolate: each compound LEAF typically has 3 (occasionally 5) leaflets, which may have little petiolules of their own; each leaflet serrate. Photo must show leaflet junction and opposite stem node to avoid treating each leaflet as an independent leaf.
morphology_keys.heads: Mostly small disk-only heads, 0–3+ rays if present, laminae ~2–3.5 mm. Outer calyculus usually 5–8(–10) ciliate green bractlets (5–20 mm, sometimes longer), INNER phyllaries normally 6–12; differentiate from vulgata's usually 10–16(–21) calyculus bractlets.
morphology_keys.fruits: Mature flattened dark cypselae, outer ~5–7 mm / inner ~7–10 mm, often 2 erect to spreading pappus awns 2–5 mm with small hooklike barbs; the FNA account notes fruit margin barbs can point forward or backward, so don't say 'always backwards.' Do not confuse awns with phyllaries or receptacular chaff.
best_field_traits: Middle stem LEAF usually divided into THREE (sometimes FIVE) separate serrated leaflets, not a single lobed blade.
Opposite leaves at each STEM NODE; look at a single petiole attached to several leaflets.
Orange-yellow disk heads with rays typically 0–3 and tiny (~2–3.5 mm).
Outer calyculus usually 5–8(–10) green bractlets, compare B. vulgata ~10–16(–21).
Inner phyllaries are a SECOND ring just behind head, not calyculus leaflets.
Flat mature outer fruit bodies ~5–7 mm, inner ~7–10 mm, generally 2 barbed awns ~2–5 mm.
FNA states marginal fruit barbs and pappus barbs may be antrorse or retrorse; not uniformly hooked backward.
Annual in wet or disturbed places, flowering commonly June–October.

comparisons.key_distinctions: B. laevis opposite SIMPLE sessile leaves + normally 7–8 large yellow rays, wet margins. B. vulgata can also have 3–5 leaflets and inconspicuous rays, but typically MORE green outer calyculus bractlets (10–16[–21] vs 5–8[–10]) and often more deeply laciniate leaves; full heads and fruits required. B. pilosa leaves may be compound and rays variable; review fruit, bracts and exact source before making a species call.
